On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿When we have died and become dust—that is a far-off return.﴾ (3) ﴿We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved Record.﴾ (4)

The objector says: no mention of the Resurrection has preceded, so that He would report of these people that they disbelieved in what they were called to. What is the sense, then, of reporting their denial of something they were not called to, and their answer to something they were not asked about? It is said: the scholars of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'Arabiyyah) have differed on this. We will mention what they said, then follow it with the explanation, God willing. Some of the grammarians of Basra said concerning it: ﴿When we have died and become dust—that is a far-off return﴾ — it does not mention that they "return"; and this, God knows best, is because it stands as an answer, as though it were said to them, "You will be returned," and they said, ﴿When we have died and become dust—that is a far-off return.﴾ Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: His words ﴿When we have died and become dust﴾ are a statement that had not appeared before it, so this cannot be its answer; rather its meaning is implied. It was, God knows best: ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an﴾ — you will certainly be resurrected after death. So they said: "When we have become dust, will we be raised?" They denied the Resurrection; then they said ﴿that is a far-off return﴾, denying it outright. His words ﴿far-off﴾ are like saying to a man who errs in a matter, "You have gone a far-off way from the right": that is, you have erred.

The correct view on this, in our opinion, is that in this speech something is omitted, the omission being dispensed with by the indication of what has been mentioned of it. God, through His report of the denial of these polytheists—whose denial of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) the surah opened by reporting—by His words ﴿Rather they marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing"﴾, threatened them for their denial of Muhammad (ﷺ). They answered the Messenger of God (ﷺ), saying ﴿When we have died and become dust﴾ — we know that, and we see what you threaten us with, in denying you — ﴿that is a far-off return﴾: that is, that this does not happen, and we will not return alive after our death. So the omission is dispensed with by the indication of His words ﴿Rather they marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves﴾, and ﴿the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing"﴾, from the mention of what you have mentioned of the report of their threat.

It has been related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿When we have died and become dust—that is a far-off return﴾: "How will God give us life again, when we have become bones and crumbled remains, and have gone astray in the earth?" This is evidence for the correctness of what we have said, that they denied the Resurrection when they were threatened with it.

*So she turned and sought with it her inward parts...
Then it fell as if it were a marij twig*

[[The verse belongs to al-Dakhil ibn Haram al-Hudhali, as in Sukkari's Sharh Ash'ar al-Hudhaliyyin, European edition, p. 269, and not to Abu Dhu'ayb, as Abu 'Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 225b). **Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 50, verses 7–8:**

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And the earth — We have spread it out, and cast therein firm mountains, and caused to grow therein every beautiful pair﴾ (7) ﴿as an insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back (to Allah)﴾ (8)

As for His words ﴿And the earth — We have spread it out﴾:

He says: We spread out the earth ﴿and cast therein firm mountains﴾, meaning: We placed in it immovable mountains, fixed firmly in the earth. ﴿And caused to grow therein every beautiful pair﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We caused to grow in the earth every kind of good plant, and this is the beautiful (bahij).

Interpreters of the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said so:

- Ali related to us, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿beautiful (bahij)﴾: it means good.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I said to Ibn Zayd, "al-bahij": is it the one pleasing to look at? He said: Yes.

He says: We did that as an insight for you, O people, by which We let you see the power of your Lord over whatever He wills. ﴿And a reminder for every servant who turns back﴾: He says: and a reminder of Allah's greatness and dominion, and an alert to His oneness, ﴿for every servant who turns back﴾: He says: for every servant who returns to faith in Allah and to acting in obedience to Him.

Interpreters of the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said so:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿an insight﴾: a blessing from Allah which the servants see. ﴿And a reminder for every servant who turns back﴾: that is, who turns with his heart to Allah.
- Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿an insight and a reminder﴾: he said, "an insight from Allah."
- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿an insight﴾: he said, "insight (basira)."

It means: So today you are one whose sight pierces through, knowing what you were heedless of in the world. It derives from their saying: "So-and-so is perceptive (basir) regarding this matter" when he has knowledge of it, and "he has insight (basar) into this matter," meaning knowledge of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 50, verses 26–28:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Who set up another god along with Allah, so cast him into the severe punishment﴾ (26)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: the one who associated others with Allah and worshipped alongside Him another object of worship from among His creation. ﴿So cast him into the severe punishment﴾ means: so cast him into the severe punishment of Hell.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿His companion will say: "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he was in far error."﴾ (27) ﴿[Allah] will say: "Do not dispute in My presence, for I had already sent to you the warning."﴾ (28)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: the companion of this human being, the disbelieving one who withholds good, who is his devil that was assigned to him in the world, will say.

As related:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿His companion will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress"﴾: "His companion is his devil."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿His companion will say﴾: "The devil was assigned to him."

* Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Who set up another god along with Allah﴾: "He is the polytheist." ﴿His companion will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress"﴾: "His companion is the devil."

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, who said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿His companion will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress"﴾: "His companion: the devil."

* It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿His companion will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress"﴾: "His companion: his devil."

* Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿His companion will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress"﴾: "His companion from the jinn: 'Our Lord, I did not make him transgress,' he disavows him."

* * *

And His saying ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress﴾

means: I did not make him a transgressor, overstepping into what is not his right; rather, it refers to disbelief in Allah. ﴿But he was in far error﴾ means: but he was on a path deviating from the way of guidance, a distant deviation.

His, the Exalted's, saying conveys this report about the words of the disbeliever's companion to him on the Day of Resurrection, to inform His servants that some of them will disavow others on the Day of Resurrection.

As related:

* Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress﴾: "He disavows him."

Those who engage in interpretation have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

* 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad related to me, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr related to us, who said: Ja'far related to us, who said: I heard Abu 'Imran say, regarding His saying ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress﴾: "He disavows him."

* * *

And His saying ﴿Do not dispute in My presence﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Allah says to these polytheists whose description and the description of their companions from the devils He has given, ﴿Do not dispute in My presence﴾ today, ﴿for I had already sent to you the warning﴾ in the world before this dispute of yours, with the threat for whoever disbelieved in Me, disobeyed Me, and opposed My command and My prohibition in My books and upon the tongues of My messengers.

Those who engage in interpretation have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

* 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad related to me, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr related to us, who said: Ja'far related to us, who said: I heard Abu 'Imran say, regarding His saying ﴿and I had already sent to you the warning﴾: "With the Qur'an."

* 'Ali related to me, who said: Abu Salih related to us, who said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Do not dispute in My presence﴾: "They offered excuses without a valid excuse, so Allah nullified their argument and rejected their statement."

* Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Do not dispute in My presence, for I had already sent to you the warning﴾: "He says: I had commanded you and forbidden you. This is the son of Adam and his companion from the jinn."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', who said: I said to Abu al-'Aliyah, "Do not dispute in My presence, for I had already sent to you the warning." Abu Ja'far al-Tabari said: I think he said: "They are the people of polytheism." And in another verse, (Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute), so they are the people of the qibla.

He said: Then another man is permitted to approach God, before him things like mountains of light, the humming of the angels' glorification is heard with him, and the clapping of their wings. The people of the Garden stretch their necks, and it is said: 'Who is this who has been permitted to approach God?' It is said: 'This is the one whom God chose for His message [[So in al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti (6:108), quoting the author. In the original it reads "bi-risalatihi", and some necessary phrases have fallen out of the original; we have placed them between these brackets.]] and brought near as a confidant, and whom Moses, peace be upon him, addressed: he has been permitted to approach God.' He said: Then another man is permitted, with him like the entire processions of the prophets before him, before him things like mountains [of light] [[So in al-Durr al-Manthur (6:108), quoting the author. Some necessary phrases have fallen out of the original; we have placed them between these brackets.]], the humming of the angels' glorification is heard with him, and the clapping of their wings. The people of the Garden stretch their necks, and it is said: 'Who is this who has been permitted to approach God?' It is said: 'This is the first intercessor, the first whose intercession is accepted, the one with the greatest number of followers at the Pool, the master of the children of Adam, the first whose grave splits open, the bearer of the banner of praise, Ahmad ﷺ, who has been permitted to approach God.' He said: The prophets then sit on pulpits of light, [the truthful ones (al-siddiqun) on couches of light, and the martyrs on chairs of light] [[So in al-Durr al-Manthur (6:108), quoting the author. Some necessary phrases have fallen out of the original; we have placed them between these brackets.]], and the rest of the people sit on mounds of pure white musk. Then the Lord, exalted is He, calls out to them from behind the veils: 'Welcome, My servants, My visitors, My neighbours, My delegation! O My angels, rise up to My servants and feed them!' He said: Then there were brought to them meat of birds, as if it were the Bukht camels, with no feathers and no bones, and they ate. He said: Then the Lord called out to them from behind the veil: 'Welcome, My servants, My visitors, My neighbours, My delegation! Let them eat; give them drink!' He said: Then there rose toward them youths like hidden pearls, with cups of gold and silver, with drinks of various and delicious kinds, whose last pleasure is like its first, neither causing headache nor intoxication. Then the Lord called out to them from behind the veils: 'Welcome, My servants, My visitors, My neighbours, My delegation! They have eaten and drunk; give them fruit!' He said: Then there is brought to them on trays crowned with rubies and coral, and of the dates which God named, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. He said: They ate, then the Lord called out to them from behind the veils: 'Welcome, My servants, My visitors, My neighbours, My delegation! They have eaten and drunk and been given fruit; clothe them!' He said: Then the fruits of the Garden were opened for them, and garments polished with the light of the Merciful were brought, and they put them on. He said: Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, called out to them from behind the veils: 'Welcome, My servants, My visitors, My neighbours, My delegation! Eat; drink; be given fruit; be clothed; be perfumed!' He said: Then there blew over them a wind called al-Muthirah, with vessels of pure white musk, and it breathed upon their faces without dust or dimness. He said: Then the Lord, mighty and majestic, called out to them from behind the veils: 'Welcome, My servants, My visitors, My neighbours, My delegation! You have eaten, drunk, been given fruit, been clothed and been perfumed. By My might, I will surely manifest Myself to them, so that they may look upon Me.' He said: That is the end of giving and the excess of the increase. He said: Then the Lord, mighty and majestic, manifested Himself to them, and then said: 'Peace be upon you, My servants; look at Me, for I am pleased with you.' He said: Then the palaces and trees of the Garden shook, [and He said:] 'Glory be to You,' four times, and the people fell down prostrate. He said: Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, called out to them: 'My servants, raise your heads, for this is not a house of works, nor a house of toil; it is only a house of recompense and reward. By My might and My majesty, I did not create it except for your sake, and there is no hour in which you remembered Me in the world except that I remembered you above My throne.'"

* Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Abjar narrated to us, saying: 'Umar ibn Yunus al-Yamami narrated to us, saying: Jahdam ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Tufayl narrated to us, saying: Abu Tayyibah narrated to me, from Mu'awiyah al-'Absi, from 'Uthman ibn 'Umayr, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me holding in his hand a white mirror, in which there was a black spot. I said: 'O Gabriel, what is this?' He said: 'This is Friday.' I said: 'And what is this black spot in it?' He said: 'It is the Hour, which will be established on a Friday, and it is the lord of the days in our sight, and we call it in the Hereafter the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazid).' I said: 'And why do you call it the Day of Increase?' He said: 'Your Lord, blessed and exalted, has made in the Garden a broad valley of pure white musk. When Friday comes, He descends from the highest places upon His Throne (kursi), then the Throne is surrounded by pulpits of light, then the prophets come and sit upon them, then the people of the Garden come and sit upon the mounds, and their Lord, mighty and majestic, manifests Himself to them, until they look upon His face. He says: "I am the One who has fulfilled My promise to you, and perfected My blessing upon you. This is the place of My honour, so ask Me." They ask Him for His pleasure. He says: "My pleasure has settled you in My abode and granted you My honour, so ask Me." They ask Him until their desire is fulfilled. Then there is opened for them at that time what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, to the extent of the people's departure from the Friday gathering, until He ascends His Throne, and the truthful ones and the martyrs ascend with Him. The people of the Garden return to their chambers, a white pearl, without a join or a break, or a red ruby, or a green emerald, whose chambers and doors are made of it. They have no greater need for anything than for the Day of Friday, so that they may increase in honour from it, and increase in looking upon His face. For this reason it is called the Day of Increase."

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from 'Uthman ibn 'Umayr, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to the hadith of Ali ibn al-Husayn.

* al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Abu Burayd, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, with something similar.

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Awn informed us, from Muhammad, who said: "We were told" or he said: "They said: the lowest of the people of the Garden in rank is the one called Tamanna (the one who wishes). His companions remind him, and he wishes, and his companions remind him, and it is said to him: 'That for you, and ten times as much with it.'" He said: Ibn 'Umar said: "That is for you, and ten times its like, and with God is more (mazid)."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that he said, from the Messenger of God ﷺ: "A man in the Garden will recline for seventy years before he shifts. Then his wife comes to him and strikes his shoulders, and he sees his face in her cheek, clearer than a mirror. The smallest pearl upon her illuminates what is between the east and the west. She greets him, he returns the greeting, and he asks her: 'Who are you?' She says: 'I am of al-Mazid.' She wears seventy garments, the least of which is like the an-Nu'man of Tuba, and his gaze penetrates them until he sees the marrow of her shin from behind all that. Upon her are crowns, and the smallest pearl among them illuminates what is between the east and the west."

* * *

And His words ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We destroyed many generations before these polytheists of Quraysh, ﴿which were stronger than them﴾ than the Quraysh who denied Muhammad, ﴿in might, and they traversed the lands﴾. He says: they split the lands and travelled through them, roaming and penetrating to their farthest regions. Imru' al-Qays said:

*"I have traversed the horizons until I was content with the spoil of returning."* [[The verse is by Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Halabi edition, p. 80), where in its version the wording is "And I have traveled (tawwaftu)" in place of "Laqad naqqabtu". Abu 'Ubaydah's version in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 226) is like the author's; he said, at the words of God "fa-naqqabu fi al-bilad": they travelled and went far; Imru' al-Qays said "Laqad naqqabtu... the verse". In Lisan al-'Arab (root n-q-b): "naqqaba fi al-ard" means he went off. In the Revelation: "fa-naqqabu fi al-bilad hal min mahis" — al-Farra' said: the readers read it with shadda, meaning they split the lands, travelling in them seeking an escape: was there for them an escape from death? He said: and whoever reads "fanqabu" with a kasra on the qaf, it is like a threat, that is, go about the lands and come back. Al-Zajjaj said: "fanqabu" means: go around, search. He said: al-Hasan read it without shadda. Imru' al-Qays said: "And I have naqqabt... the verse," meaning I struck in the lands, I came and went. End of quotation.]]

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

* 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿and they traversed the lands﴾: "They left their mark."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and they traversed the lands﴾: "He says: they worked in the lands that digging (naqb)."

Those who said that:

* * *

And His words ﴿Is there any escape?﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: Was there for them, by their roaming in the lands, any way of escape from death, or any deliverance from destruction when Our command came upon them?

The word "kana" (was) has been left implied in this place, as it is implied in His words ﴿And how many a town, stronger in power than your town which expelled you, We destroyed, and there was no helper for them﴾, meaning: there was no helper for them when they were destroyed. The readers (al-qurra') read His words ﴿fa-naqqabu﴾ with shadda and a fatha on the qaf, as a report about them. It is reported from Yahya ibn Ya'mur that he read it ﴿fa-naqqibu﴾ with a kasra on the qaf, as a threat and warning: that is, roam the lands and move about in them, for you will never escape Us by yourselves.

And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿mahis﴾.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them﴾ ... until ﴿Is there any escape?﴾: "The wicked fled, and found the command of God pursuing them."

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿fa-naqqabu fi al-bilad, hal min mahis﴾: "The enemies of God fled, and found the command of God overtaking them."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Is there any escape?﴾: "Is there any deliverer?"

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or gives ear while he is a witness﴾ (50:37)

His saying, exalted is He, means: Indeed in Our destroying the generations whom We destroyed before the Quraysh there is ﴿a reminder﴾ by which one may take heed ﴿for whoever has a heart﴾, meaning: for whoever among this community has intellect, so that he refrains from the deed they used to commit through their disbelief in their Lord, out of fear that there may befall him the like of the punishment that befell them.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying (Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart): i.e., from this community, meaning by "heart" the living heart.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿for whoever has a heart﴾, he said: whoever has a heart from this community.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿for whoever has a heart﴾, he said: a heart that comprehends what has been heard of the reports of the nations which Allah struck with which those who disobeyed Him. The "heart" in this place is the intellect. It is from their saying: "Fulan has no heart, and his heart is not with him," meaning his intellect is not with him. And where has your heart gone? meaning where has your intellect gone?

* *

And His saying ﴿or gives ear while he is a witness﴾

He says: or he listens, with his hearing, to Our report to him about these generations whom We destroyed, so that he hears the report about them, how We dealt with them when they disbelieved in their Lord and disobeyed their messengers. ﴿while he is a witness﴾ means: while he is attentive to what is reported about them, a witness to it with his heart, not heedless of it nor inattentive.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this, though their wording differed.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or gives ear while he is a witness﴾, he says: if he listens to the reminder and witnesses its command, he says concerning that: it suffices him if he understands it. [[As in the original; the likely correct wording is: "indeed that suffices him if he understands it."]]

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿or gives ear﴾, he said: and he does not speak to himself; a witnessing heart.

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿or gives ear while he is a witness﴾: The Arabs say: "Fulan gave ear (alqa al-sam')," meaning he listened with his ears, and "he is a witness" means: not absent.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or gives ear while he is a witness﴾, he said: he hears what is said, while his heart is elsewhere than what he hears.

Others said: by "the witness" in this place is meant: the testimony.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, ﴿or gives ear while he is a witness﴾, meaning by that the People of the Book, who witness, concerning what is recited in the Book of Allah, the sending of Muhammad ﷺ.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿or gives ear while he is a witness﴾: a witness to what is in his hand of the Book of Allah, that he finds the Prophet ﷺ written down.

He said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar said, and al-Hasan said: it is a hypocrite who listens to the speech but does not benefit from it.

Ahmad ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa told us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿or gives ear while he is a witness﴾, he said: the believer hears the Qur'an, and he is a witness to it.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿or gives ear while he is a witness﴾, he said: "gives ear" means he hears what has been reported, of the reports about the past nations, though he did not witness them, how Allah punished them and what He did to them when they disobeyed His messengers.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 38:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: And We certainly created the seven heavens and the earth, and what is between them of creatures, in six days, and no weariness touched Us.

As follows:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Abu Bakr, who said: The Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, tell us what God created of creation in these six days?" He said: "God created the earth on Sunday and Monday, and He created the mountains on Tuesday, and He created the cities, the sustenance, the rivers, their cultivation and their ruin on Wednesday, and He created the heavens and the angels on Thursday until three hours [remained] of Friday, and He created in the first of those three hours the due terms, and in the second the calamity, and in the third Adam." They said: "You have spoken truly, if you complete [the account]." The Prophet (ﷺ) understood what they intended, so he became angry, and God revealed: ﴿And no fatigue touched Us, so be patient over what they say﴾.

Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿and no fatigue touched Us﴾, he said: from weariness.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and no fatigue touched Us﴾, he said: from exhaustion [al-izhaf]. [Al-izhaf: al-i'ya', meaning weariness, which has the same meaning as al-lughub (Lisan al-Arab: zahf).]

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and no fatigue touched Us﴾, he says: and no toil touched Us.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and no fatigue touched Us﴾, he said: toil.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth﴾... the verse: God refuted the Jews, the Christians and the people of falsehood who fabricate against God, for they said: God created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rested on the seventh day, and that for them is Saturday, which they call the day of rest.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿from fatigue﴾: The Jews said: God created the heavens and the earth in six days, finished the creation on Friday, and rested on Saturday. So God refuted them and said ﴿and no fatigue touched Us﴾.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾: the measure of each day was a thousand years of what you count.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and no fatigue touched Us﴾: there did not touch Us in that any hardship, that is fatigue.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 39–40:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and exalt your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting. (39) And of the night, glorify Him, and [also] after the prostrations.﴾ (40)

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "So be patient, O Muhammad, over what these Jews say, and what they fabricate against God and lie about Him, for God is ever watchful over them." ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun﴾: that is, pray with praise to your Lord, the dawn prayer before the sunrise, and the afternoon prayer before the sunset.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah (﴿And exalt your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun﴾): this is for the dawn prayer, and before its setting: the afternoon prayer.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before the setting﴾: "Before the rising of the sun": the dawn prayer; and "before the setting": the afternoon prayer.

* * *

As for His words ﴿And of the night, glorify Him﴾:

The people of interpretation differed concerning the glorification He commanded from the night. Some of them said: it refers to the prayer of ʿAtamah (the night prayer, i.e. ʿishaʾ).

Those who said this:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And of the night﴾: "It is the ʿAtamah." Others said: it is prayer during the night, at whatever time one prays.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn ʿUmarah al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: ʿUbaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Israʾil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid (﴿And of the night, glorify Him﴾): "Of the night, all of it."

The view stated by Mujahid is closer to the truth, because God, exalted is His praise, said ﴿And of the night, glorify Him﴾ and did not limit a particular time of the night over another. When this is so, it applies to all hours of the night. Given that the matter is as we have described, it is more fitting that it be a command to the maghrib and ʿishaʾ prayers than that it be a command to the ʿAtamah prayer, since both of them are prayed at night.

* * *

As for His words ﴿and after the prostrations﴾:

He says: glorify your Lord with praise after the prostrations of your prayer.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the glorification which God commanded His Prophet to perform after the prostrations. Some of them said: it refers to the prayer, and they said: these are the two rak'ahs prayed after the maghrib prayer.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: ʿAnbasah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, who said: I asked ʿAli about "adbar al-sujud" (the afterparts of the prostrations), and he said: "The two rak'ahs after the maghrib."

* Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: ʿAli (may God be pleased with him) said regarding ﴿adbar al-sujud﴾: "The two rak'ahs after the maghrib."

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Musʿab ibn Sallam narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, who said: I heard ʿAli (may God be pleased with him) say ﴿adbar al-sujud﴾: "The two rak'ahs after the maghrib."

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from ʿAli (may God be pleased with him), regarding His words ﴿and after the prostrations﴾: "The two rak'ahs after the maghrib."

* He said: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from ʿAsim ibn Damrah, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli (may God be pleased with them both), who said: ﴿adbar al-sujud﴾: "The two rak'ahs after the maghrib."

* ʿAli ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, saying: ʿAli ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Aws ibn Khalid, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Adbar al-sujud: two rak'ahs after the maghrib prayer."

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAlwan ibn Abi Malik, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: "Adbar al-sujud: the two rak'ahs after the maghrib."

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, and Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid (﴿adbar al-sujud﴾): "The two rak'ahs after the maghrib."

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Ibrahim, the same.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Ibrahim regarding this verse ﴿And of the night, glorify Him, and adbar al-sujud﴾ and ﴿wa-idbar al-nujum (and the retreat of the stars)﴾: "The two rak'ahs before dawn, and the two rak'ahs after the maghrib." Shuʿbah said: "I do not know which of them is adbar al-sujud, and I do not know which of them is idbar al-nujum."

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and adbar al-sujud﴾: Mujahid used to say: "Two rak'ahs after the maghrib."

* Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿and adbar al-sujud﴾: "They are the two prostrations after the maghrib prayer."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 41–42:

The explanation of His saying, ﴿And listen, on the day the caller calls from a near place, (41) the day they hear the Shout in truth. That is the Day of Coming Out (42)﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And listen, O Muhammad, to the Shout of the Day of Resurrection, the day on which Our caller calls with it from a near place.

It is mentioned that it will be called out from the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

Mention of those who said that:

Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from Ka'b, who said: ﴿And listen, on the day the caller calls from a near place﴾ "An angel standing on the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis calls: O you decayed bones and scattered joints, indeed Allah commands you to gather for the judgment of decision."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And listen, on the day the caller calls from a near place﴾ He said: "We used to be told that it will be called from Bayt al-Maqdis, from the rock, which is the middle of the earth."

And we were told that Ka'b said: "It is the nearest part of the earth to the heaven, by eighteen miles."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿on the day the caller calls from a near place﴾ He said: "It reached me that it will be called from the rock that is in Bayt al-Maqdis."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And listen, on the day the caller calls from a near place﴾ He said: "It is the Shout."

Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: some of our companions narrated to me, from al-Aghurr, from Muslim ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father Buraydah, who said: "An angel standing on the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis, with his two fingers in his ears, calls." He said: I said: "With what does he call?" He said: "He says: O people, come to the reckoning." He said: "So they come, as Allah said: ﴿as if they were scattered locusts﴾."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿the day they hear the Shout in truth﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the day on which the creatures hear the Shout of resurrection from the graves in truth, meaning by the command to answer Allah, to the place of reckoning.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿That is the Day of Coming Out﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the day of the people of the graves coming out of their graves.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return (43) On the Day the earth will split asunder from them, [they will emerge] hastening. That is a gathering, easy for Us.﴾ (44)

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed, We are the One who gives life to the dead and causes the living to die, and to Us is the final return of all of them on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿On the Day the earth will split asunder from them, [they will emerge] hastening﴾. He, whose praise is majestic, says: and to Us is their return on the Day the earth splits; so "the Day" is connected to "return" (maṣīr).

* *

As for His words ﴿the earth will split asunder from them﴾:

He says: the earth will burst open from them.

* *

As for His words ﴿hastening﴾:

"Hastening" (sirā'an) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of the pronoun in His words "from them". The meaning is: on the Day the earth splits open from them, they will come out of it hastening. It suffices, by the indication of His words "on the Day the earth splits open from them", that this is what is meant.

* *

As for His words ﴿That is a gathering, easy for Us﴾:

He says: that gathering of them is a gathering to the place of reckoning, and it is easy and simple for Us.

He, the Exalted, says: We know best, O Muhammad, what these polytheists who associate others with Allah say of falsehood against Allah, their denial of His signs, and their denial of Allah's power to resurrect after death.

As it was said:

Ḥaddathanī Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, qāla: thanā Abū ʿĀṣim, qāla: thanā ʿĪsā, and Ḥaddathanī al-Ḥārith, qāla: thanā al-Ḥasan, qāla: thanā Warqāʾ, all of them, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding ﴿And you are not over them a compeller﴾, he said: "Do not domineer over them."

Ḥaddathanā Bishr, qāla: thanā Yazīd, qāla: thanā Saʿīd, from Qatādah, regarding His words ﴿And you are not over them a compeller﴾: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disliked compulsion (al-jabriyyah), forbade it, and warned against it. And al-Farrāʾ said: the word jabbār was placed in the position of sulṭān (authority) from jabriyyah; and he said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:

"And on the Day of al-Ḥazn, when Maʿadd gathered,
and the people, other than us, were submissive.
We disobeyed the decree of the compeller until
we attacked al-Jawf with a thousand marked men."

The first verse was previously cited by the author at His words "Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam" (2:211) in this edition. The point of citation here is in the second verse, in the word "jabbār," meaning the dominant ruler.
